title: Making comfrey liquid feed
subtitle: A high-potassium feed from cut leaves and water, ready in four weeks.
excerpt: Comfrey liquid feed is made by steeping cut leaves in water until they break down into a dark, nutrient-rich concentrate. It is particularly high in potassium, making it useful for fruiting crops like tomatoes, courgettes, and peppers.
sourceNotes: Nutrient composition after Lawrence Hills, Comfrey: Past, Present and Future (1976). Brewing method after Garden Organic guidance. Dilution ratios widely used in UK organic kitchen gardening.

glossaryTerms.definition: A liquid or granular feed high in potassium (K), which supports flower and fruit development in plants. Comfrey and seaweed are the main organic sources.

content.text: Comfrey liquid feed is a dark, smelly concentrate made by stuffing cut comfrey leaves into a barrel of water and leaving them to rot down. The result is a
suitable for tomatoes, peppers, courgettes, squash, and any other fruiting crop. It is free to make from Bocking 14 comfrey grown in the garden.
A full batch takes about four weeks to brew. The feed keeps for up to a year in a sealed container in a cool, dark place, though the smell does not improve with age.

items.name: Comfrey leaves (fresh cut)
items.qty: as many as you have; 1 kg fills a 10-litre bucket

items.name: Bucket or barrel with lid
items.qty: 10 to 30 litres; a lid reduces the smell

items.name: Brick or stone
items.qty: to weigh the leaves under the water

items.name: Rubber gloves
items.qty: optional but recommended; the liquid stains skin and smells strongly

content.text: Cut comfrey leaves and pack them into the bucket. Fill the bucket with water to cover the leaves, then weigh them down with a brick or flat stone so they stay submerged. Cover with a lid or a sheet of cardboard to reduce evaporation and smell. Leave for four weeks in a warm spot.

After four weeks, the leaves have broken down into a black or dark brown sludge. Strain the liquid into bottles or cans through an old piece of sacking or a coarse strainer. The remaining sludge goes on the compost heap or dug into a trench.

attrs.title: The concentrate method
attrs.body: For a more concentrated feed, pack the bucket with comfrey leaves and add no water. The leaves break down under their own weight into a small amount of very dark concentrate over 4 to 6 weeks. This can be drilled from a hole in the bottom of a bucket set over a collection container. Dilute this concentrate 1:20 before using.

content.text: Dilute the liquid feed 1:10 with water before applying. It should look like weak tea. Apply directly to the soil around fruiting plants once a week from when the first flowers appear through to the end of the harvest season.
Do not apply neat: the concentrate is strong enough to scorch roots. Do not apply to seedlings or young transplants in their first week after planting.

Three to five established comfrey plants yield enough leaves for four to six cuts per season, producing 20 to 30 litres of undiluted feed. Diluted 1:10, this is 200 to 300 litres of ready-to-use feed. That is enough to feed a medium kitchen garden through a full growing season.
